Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 20. Levofloxacin is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as quinolone antibiotics. 21. This antibiotic treats bacterial infections only and will not work for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. 22. Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting levofloxacin and each time you get a refill. 23. Take this medication by mouth on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after eating) as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. 24. Take this medication at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after taking other products that may reduce its effectiveness, such as quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals (including iron and zinc), and products containing magnesium, aluminum, or calcium (e.g., antacids, calcium-enriched juice). 25. Carefully measure the dose using a special measuring device or spoon. 26. The dosage and length of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to treatment. 27. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. 28. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. 29. Common side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, or trouble sleeping. 30. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 31. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. 32. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. 33. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. 34. Before taking levofloxacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other quinolone antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, moxifloxacin, ofloxacin), or any other allergies. 35. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. 36. Levofloxacin may cause a condition affecting the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). 37. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. 38. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase the risk of QT prolongation. 39. This risk may increase if you use certain drugs (e.g., diuretics or water pills) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. 40. Levofloxacin may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, especially if you have diabetes. 41. Watch for symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. 42. Also, watch for symptoms of low blood sugar, such as sudden sweating, shaking, fast heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling hands/feet. 43. It is advisable to carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar. If unavailable, quickly raise your blood sugar by consuming sugar, honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda. 44. Inform your doctor immediately about any reactions and the use of this product. 45. To prevent low blood sugar, eat meals on a regular schedule and do not skip meals. 46. This drug may cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. 47.
